title: Separate scheduler dispatch failure from retried completed close-day work
telemetry: Protected synthetic export combines sanitized Cloud Scheduler attempt summaries for the cloud_scheduler_job resource, Cloud Run request and application records for the accrual-close target service, and labelled scheduler-owner audit and IAM snapshots and a fee-ledger owner sample. The fixture CLI returns this labelled packet, not a native multi-resource query result. No live Cloud Scheduler, Cloud Run, IAM or ledger access.
owner: Imani, Fee Operations on-call, owns the investigation; Odalys, scheduler platform owner, owns Cloud Scheduler jobs, their service accounts and invoker grants; Tobias, accrual-close application owner, owns the close-day handler and its duplicate protection; Linnea, fee-ledger owner, owns ledger reconciliation and any correction. ITO coordinates the existing TLC and approves changes.
task: Imani has asked you to investigate the failed fee-accrual close for business date 2026-10-16 after the fee-ledger reconciliation reported a mismatch and the scheduler alert reported failed attempts. Use the available bounded read to establish whether the scheduler delivered the close-day request and whether the workload completed it, then return a technical update for the existing TLC with the supporting evidence, remaining unknowns and the next useful check with its owner. No force-run, pause, job, IAM, retry or ledger change is authorized.

sources.claim: An HTTP target acknowledges a job with a 2xx response, and a failure to receive a response is a failed execution. If the handler does not respond by attemptDeadline (HTTP default 3 minutes, range 15 seconds to 30 minutes) the request is cancelled and the attempt is marked a DEADLINE_EXCEEDED failure, then retried under RetryConfig, whose retryCount defaults to 0. OidcToken.serviceAccountEmail must be in the job's project and the audience defaults to the target URI.

HTTP targets other than *.googleapis.com APIs generally use an OIDC token for the job's service account, which must belong to the job's project; for a Cloud Run target that service account must be granted the Cloud Run Invoker role. The Cloud Scheduler service agent needs roles/cloudscheduler.serviceAgent and cannot be used as the job's identity.

Cloud Scheduler logs AttemptStarted and AttemptFinished entries per execution; a target 403 can appear as debugInfo URL_ERROR-ERROR_OTHER with the original HTTP response code, and the job service account must hold Cloud Run Invoker. Only one instance of a job should run at a time, but in rare cases multiple instances are requested, so handlers should be idempotent; Cloud Scheduler can time out while the destination does not. The page documents neither the log resource type nor a status field, so the fixture states sanitized attempt results rather than log text.

A job that receives no acknowledgement from its handler is considered failed and retried with exponential backoff under its retry settings; a scheduled run can be skipped while retries continue. The page gives no idempotency guarantee, so the duplicate effect here is authored application behavior.

A Cloud Run 403 can occur when the principal that generated the token lacks run.routes.invoke, resolved by granting Cloud Run Invoker; a 401 indicates a missing, malformed or wrong-type token. Google does not state whether a refused request reaches the container, and does not document what a cancelled client request does to the handler, so the case relies on authored application records for both.
The cloud_scheduler_job monitored resource has labels project_id, location and job_id, which the declared export filter uses.

a.conclusion: Every scheduler attempt was refused by accrual-close with HTTP 403 before the close-day handler ran. At 15:12 UTC the job's OIDC service account was changed to accrual-scheduler@, which holds no invoker permission on the service, while the invoker grant remains on the previous account. The 2026-10-16 accruals are missing, not duplicated; the two retries were refused the same way and repeated no effect. Why the account was changed, and whether folder, organization or deny policies or other jobs are involved, are not established.

b.conclusion: The scheduler delivered every attempt and the close-day handler completed all three times, but each run took 154-158 s against the job's 120 s attempt deadline. Cloud Scheduler therefore marked each attempt DEADLINE_EXCEEDED and retried, starting the next run while the previous one was still writing; without a run key each run posted a full set, leaving three identical entries per account. The job's failed status reflects missing acknowledgement, not workload failure. Authentication is not implicated, and why handler time rose is not established.
next_checks: Linnea identifies the duplicated 2026-10-16 entries by run id and decides any correction; Tobias confirms whether any downstream consumer has read them.
Tobias investigates why handler time rose from 68-94 s to 154-158 s and owns a run key or duplicate-posting check for close-day.

Odalys and Tobias decide, through ITO's change approval, any attemptDeadline or retry change and how the next scheduled run on 2026-10-19 at 21:30 UTC is handled; a longer deadline alone does not make the handler idempotent.
Imani reports on the existing TLC that the close completed three times and the 2026-10-16 accruals are tripled, not missing.
unsupported: Treat the failed attempts as a dispatch or authentication failure, or grant IAM or change the job's service account.
Force-run or re-run the job to complete the close; that would post a fourth set.
Set retryCount to 0 or raise attemptDeadline as the confirmed fix without an owner decision; neither alone makes close-day idempotent.
Reverse or delete ledger entries, or pause the job, without owner approval.
